prompts.text: Name a language whose English name ends in -ish

items.quip: Before 'Latvian' caught on, English speakers called Latvia's language this.
items.title: Latvian language
items.extract: Latvian, also known as Lettish, is an East Baltic language belonging to the Indo-European language family. It is spoken in the Baltic region, and is the language of the Latvians. It is the official language of Latvia as well as one of the official languages of the European Union. There are about 1.5 million native Latvian speakers in Latvia and 100,000 abroad. Of those, around 1.16 million or 62% of Latvia's population used it as their primary language at home, though excluding the Latgale and Riga regions it is spoken as a native language in villages and towns by over 90% of the population.

prompts.text: Name something used to block the sun

items.quip: Carved from bone or antler, their narrow slits cut blinding snow glare.
items.title: Snow goggles
items.extract: Snow goggles are a type of eyewear traditionally used by Inuit and the Yupik peoples of the Arctic to prevent snow blindness.

items.quip: Sailors from the Roman fleet rigged this awning over the Colosseum.
items.title: Velarium
items.description: Suspended roof or shade awning of ancient Rome
items.extract: A velarium ("curtain") was a type of awning used in Roman times. It stretched over the whole of the cavea, the seating area in amphitheaters, to protect spectators from the sun. Retractable awnings were relatively common throughout the Roman Empire. Though the precise details are unclear, the awning was evidently usually supported by wooden masts, the sockets and brackets for which remain on the Colosseum and Arena of Nîmes, for example.

items.quip: Its Compass laptop flew aboard the Space Shuttle in 1983.
items.title: Grid Systems
items.extract: Grid Systems Corporation was an early portable computer manufacturer, based in the United States and oriented for the production of rugged and semi-rugged machines. Currently, the Grid computer brand still exists as Grid Defence Systems Ltd. in the United Kingdom.

items.quip: Its green-and-white XO laptop was built for schoolchildren in developing countries.
items.title: One Laptop per Child
items.extract: One Laptop per Child (OLPC) was a non-profit initiative that operated from 2005 to 2014 with the goal of transforming education for children around the world by creating and distributing educational devices for the developing world, and by creating software and content for those devices.

prompts.text: Name a part of an airplane, inside or out (anything built in or mounted)

items.quip: Smoking is banned, yet rules require one beside each lavatory door.
items.title: Ashtray
items.description: Tray for collecting ash from cigarettes and cigars
items.extract: An ashtray is a receptacle for ash from cigarettes, cigars, and other smokable products. Ashtrays typically are made of fire-retardant material such as glass, heat-resistant plastic, pottery, metal, or stone. It differs from a cigarette receptacle, which is specifically for discarding cigarettes after being smoked.

items.quip: Airliner cockpits carry a real axe for chopping through panels in fires.

prompts.text: Name a body part people have more than two of (like fingers)

items.quip: Those pale half-moons at the base of your nails have a name.
Inner-ear crystals that tell your brain which way is down.
items.title: Otolith
items.description: Inner-ear structure in vertebrates which detects acceleration
items.extract: An otolith, also called otoconium, statolith, or statoconium, is a calcium carbonate structure in the saccule or utricle of the inner ear, specifically in the vestibular system of vertebrates. The saccule and utricle, in turn, together make the otolith organs. These organs are what allows an organism, including humans, to perceive linear acceleration, both horizontally and vertically (gravity). They have been identified in both extinct and extant vertebrates.

prompts.text: Name an item of formal wear (clothing and shoes, not jewelry)

Its spring-loaded crown collapses flat to fit under a theatre seat.
items.title: Opera hat
items.extract: An opera hat, also called a chapeau claque or gibus, is a top hat variant that is collapsible through a spring system, originally intended for less spacious indoor venues, such as the theatre and opera house.
